newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end thin bourse dealings lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end thin bourse dealings lower.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade down on Monday as floor dealings caught up with losses made during late Friday electronic dealings and weaker German bonds weighed on the market.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares ended down 11.39 points, or 0.42 percent, down at 2,671.86.
After the close of floor dealings on Friday, the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index, had fallen as profits were taken on the bond markets.
Dealers said they saw the DAX index making no dramatic moves ahead of the U.S. elections on Tuesday, but said it was also well-supported around current levels.
Although the U.S. election will be the week's main focus, a flurry of German data and company results was also likely to keep the market entertained.

Amongst the results expected were car maker Daimler's nine month figures, due out on Thursday. Daimler shares, which were popular last week, continued to rise, gaining 34 pfennigs to end bourse trade at 90.75 marks.
Shares in car maker Volkswagen also benefited from interest in the auto industry, rising 3.25 marks to 613.25 marks.
The main market-moving news was the confirmation over the weekend of the merger between British Telecommunications Plc and U.S firm MCI Communications.
German mixed utility Viag AG, BT's partner in Germany, climbed nearly one percent, or five marks to 570.50 marks.
German utility competitors, Veba and RWE, both in alliance with the British Cable and Wireless, were little moved on the news.
RWE gained 15 pfennigs to trade at 63.15 marks, while Veba lost 30 pfennigs to stand at 81.30 marks.
Meanwhile preference shares in business software firm SAP AG continues to slip after a profits warning issued two weeks ago. The shares were down 3.70 marks at 191.80 marks.
